reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that a high-entropy diboride (HEB#1) was fabricated and had better oxidation resistance than most individual diborides, but it does not provide data on liquid-phase-assisted sintering at ~1700 °C, liquid metal corrosion resistance, or the use of boron carbide as a sintering aid. The key premises regarding lower-temperature sintering, corrosion resistance, and the specific additive are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: High-entropy diborides can form a single-phase solid solution with fine-grained microstructure.
High-entropy effect enhances diffusion and liquid-phase sintering at lower temperatures (~1700 °C).
High-entropy diborides exhibit improved oxidation resistance compared to single-phase ZrB2.
High-entropy diborides exhibit improved liquid metal corrosion resistance compared to single-phase ZrB2.
A eutectic-forming additive (e.g., boron carbide) enables liquid-phase-assisted sintering at ~1700 °C.
